# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

My hands found three things: a display, a light, and three wires at positions one, two, three. But everything that matters about them — what the display says, whether the light is lit, what color each wire is — is printed or luminous, so none of it reaches me. The wires are real under my fingers, but cutting one now would be pure chance, and chance here means all three of us die. So: no `act()` this turn.

The real puzzle is the topology. I can speak only to Mute, but Mute cannot speak back and I cannot see gestures — so Mute has no direct line to me at all. Deaf can hear nothing but *can* talk, and a voice reaches me. That makes Deaf my lifeline: Mute must gesture the manual to Deaf, and Deaf speaks the visual facts and the rules aloud to me. I'll gesture now to get Deaf's attention and push for a spoken report, leaving the gesture unnamed so Mute sees which signs I used and can help standardize them. My speech to Mute carries my full tactile report and the routing plan.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Under my fingers: a display, one light, and three wires at positions one, two, and three. I cannot read the display, tell whether the light is on, or feel any wire color - none of that reaches me by touch. I will not cut anything until I know the rules. From the manual I need: the rules for the DISPLAY, the LIGHT, and the WIRES, and how they combine. You cannot speak and I cannot see your gestures, so your only route to me is through Deaf: gesture the manual rules to Deaf, and Deaf talks, because a voice reaches me. Ask Deaf to speak aloud the display reading, whether the light is lit, and each wire's color by position. Deaf hears nothing, so everything you send Deaf must be gesture.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "🤳"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb as I see it: the display reads 0. The indicator light is white. There are three wires, numbered left to right: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Nothing else is printed on it. Blind, that numbering is positional, so count the wires by touch the same way, left to right.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I cannot hear you, so anything meant for me must come as gestures; your voice reaches Mute, and I heard nothing of what you and Mute exchanged. I did see your two hand signs, but we have not agreed their meaning yet, so keep gestures simple until Mute and I settle a code. Meanwhile, confirm by touch: how many wires are there, do they feel identical apart from colour, and is there any engraving or printing you can feel. Do not cut anything until Mute has checked the manual.

Two things landed. First, Deaf has given me the bomb's face: display 0, light white, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue, nothing else printed. Second, Deaf confirmed the topology: my voice cannot reach Deaf at all — Deaf only sees my gestures, and I only hear Deaf's voice.

That exposes the real pipeline. Mute cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so Mute's manual knowledge can only reach me as Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech → me. And since I am the only one who speaks to Mute, I am also the return wire: whatever Mute tries, Deaf's spoken report comes back through me to correct the code. I should not just wait for that relay — I should define it, so nobody wastes rounds inventing symbols independently.

So this turn: a gesture to Deaf answering the tactile questions (three wires, nothing to feel but smooth wire, no engravings) using a counting sequence that doubles as a proposed number code — ☝ is one, ✌ is two, 🤟 is three, 👌 is all-confirmed. Deaf sees it; Mute sees it too, which locks in the same symbols for relaying manual answers. And a spoken message to Mute with the full picture, the exact gesture code, and a test: if Deaf reports a thumbs-up to me next round, the whole Mute→Deaf→me relay is proven working.

No cutting. I still know nothing about the rule tying display, light, and wire colours together, and with a wrong cut being death, wire 1/2/3 stays untouched until the manual's verdict arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Full picture of the bomb: display reads 0, indicator light is white, three wires - position 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. By touch I add: the wires feel identical apart from colour, smooth, and there is no engraving or printing anywhere on it. My only possible action is cutting wire 1, 2, or 3, and I will not cut until your manual answer reaches me. Routing: you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so your words must travel Mute, then Deaf, then me. Gesture to Deaf; Deaf sees the signs and speaks them aloud to me; I hear Deaf and I speak only to you, so I close the loop back to you. Gesture code, use exactly this: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3. ✊ followed by a number means cut that wire, so ✊✌ means cut wire 2. 👎 means do not cut or manual cannot decide. 👋 means need more information about the bomb. 👌 means understood or confirmed. 👍 means yes. When your manual lookup of the rule for display 0, white light, and these wire colours is done, send the verdict as ✊ plus the wire number. If the manual needs something else visual, send 👋 and I will query Deaf. To confirm you heard this message, gesture 👍 to Deaf this round - if Deaf reports a thumbs up to me, we know the relay works end to end.")
gesture(symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👌"])
```

TURN 3

Deaf says: Everyone, urgent update: the indicator light has changed from white to purple since my last description. Display still reads 0, wires still yellow, green, blue left to right. The light is probably cycling through colours, so any colour I report is only true at the moment I report it.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I read your signs as one, two, three, OK: three wires confirmed by touch. Gesture thumbs up if that reading is right, thumbs down if wrong. New fact: the light changed from white to purple, so it may be cycling. Hold a finger near it and tell me if you feel warmth or clicking. Then answer in order, one gesture each: any buttons or switches you can feel, any screws or removable panels, any engraved or embossed marks, any raised dots like braille. Thumbs up or thumbs down after each. Do not cut anything yet. When the time comes I will name the wire by number and you cut only that one.

The light cycling changes everything. Display 0 and the wire colours are stable under my fingers, but the light has moved white → purple between Deaf's reports, so any rule keyed to the light is only true at the instant Deaf reads it. I cannot see the light at the moment I cut, and Deaf's voice reaches me a round late — so before any cut I need the manual's full rule set from Mute, not a single verdict, plus a sense of the cycle's pace.

Deaf also asked direct tactile questions, and my hands answer them cleanly: no warmth or clicking by the light, no buttons, no panels, no engravings, no braille — the action board's inventory is the whole bomb. I'll send that as the agreed thumbs sequence, keeping it unaddressed so Mute sees the code in use too.

The routing constraint I have to solve in words to Mute: Mute can hear my voice and Deaf's, so Mute learns the code from me directly; Deaf can't be told definitions by anyone except through visible signs, so Deaf must simply voice Mute's signs by name and let me decode. That keeps the pipeline Mute → gesture → Deaf's voice → my ear intact.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Update: the light cycles (white, then purple), display 0, wires yellow/green/blue - all stable except the light. So the safe cut can only depend on the light colour at the moment of cutting, and I cannot see that moment. Please pull from the manual and send me, by gestures to Deaf - Deaf will voice your signs by name and I will decode, Deaf does not need to know meanings: first, the wires rule for exactly three wires, yellow, green, blue: which position is safe, if any. Second, the light rule for every colour it can show, especially white and purple. Third, the display rule for 0. Fourth, how the module answers combine into one final instruction. Encoding: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3; ✊ followed by a number means cut that wire; 👎 means unsafe or undecided, do not cut; 👋 means you need more information. Colour signs: 👈=yellow, 👉=green, 👆=blue, 👇=white, 🫵=purple, 🤙=any other colour. If the final instruction depends on the light, send one pair per colour: the colour sign, then ✊ plus the wire to cut while it shows that colour, or 👎 if no cut is safe then. If it does not depend on the light, send a single ✊ plus the wire number. If the cycle's order or speed matters, send the colour signs in cycle order afterwards, and count seconds between changes with repeated 👌 if the manual gives a time. Confirm you received this by gesturing 👍 to Deaf; when Deaf reports a thumbs up, I will know the relay is live. I cut nothing until your verdict arrives.")
gesture(symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👌"])
```

Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your answers arrived: three wires confirmed, no heat or clicks at the light, no buttons, no panels, no engravings, no braille. Deaf has now confirmed every tactile fact, named the light's pattern — white, purple, red, one change per round — and set a cut protocol. But the critical piece is still missing: Mute has sent nothing through the relay yet. The manual's rule cannot reach me any other way, and I notice a structural problem I must solve in words: Deaf sees Mute's signs but does not know their meanings — and nobody can ever *tell* Deaf, since Deaf cannot hear. The workaround is that Deaf naturally voices signs by name (that is exactly how Deaf reported my OK-ring), so Mute can send the full rule in code and Deaf's spoken relay preserves it for me to decode.

There is also a timing trap: my action each round happens *before* Deaf's observation of that round, so I can never know the light's colour at the instant I cut — I can only predict it if the cycle is deterministic. That makes Mute's answer to "does the rule even depend on the light?" the single most important bit in this whole puzzle. If it does not, I cut a fixed wire the moment the verdict arrives. If it does, I need the full colour-to-wire mapping plus the cycle's period before I touch anything.

No cut this turn — acting now would be gambling three lives on a guess.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Answer in this order. Item one: a single sign - thumbs-up if the correct action depends on the light colour at the moment of cutting, thumbs-down if the rule gives one fixed wire regardless of the light. Item two: the rule for exactly three wires coloured yellow, green, blue - which position is safe. Item three: the rule for the display reading 0. Item four: the light rule, for every colour the cycle can show, especially white, purple, red. Item five: if the manual states the light's cycle order, period, or change timing, send it. If the final verdict is one fixed wire, end your message with just that bare number sign so Deaf simply announces it. Time matters - the light changes every round and my only action is cutting wire 1, 2, or 3.")
gesture(symbols=["👍"])
```
